plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms that unfurl in the cool of winter. Their waxy petals surround a bright boss of golden stamens, and the flowers stand out against dark, polished leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, peaking in midwinter to early spring
plants.location: Gardens and woodlands of southern Japan, and mild-winter regions such as the southeastern United States and coastal Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. In Japan the species has been cultivated and admired for centuries, and thousands of cultivars now exist.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bold bulb with trumpet-shaped, outward-facing blooms held on tall, sturdy stems. In the warm southern summer the flowers burn bright against lush foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering often extending through midsummer
plants.location: Tropical and subtropical Americas, widely grown in warm gardens in Australia and South Africa
plants.funFact: Hippeastrum is often called amaryllis. The name Amaryllis technically belongs to a different genus from South Africa, a mix-up botanists have debated for more than two centuries.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A gnarled, graceful tree that flowers on bare branches while winter still grips the landscape. Its fragrant blossoms open in the cold, and their sweet scent drifts through plum gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to early spring, often starting in January in mild regions
plants.location: Mild-winter parts of Japan and China, including coastal and lowland plum groves
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture because they bloom in the harshest part of winter. The fruit is pickled into the Japanese umeboshi.
